pointers.sentence: Before any middleware runs, the handler does the same four things for every request, in this order: it keeps the script prefix, sends the `request_started` signal, makes the request object, and calls `BaseHandler.get_response`, which sets the URLconf and calls the chain (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIHandler.__call__`, `django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.get_response`).

Before any middleware runs, the handler does the same four things for every request, in this order: it keeps the script prefix, sends the `request_started` signal, makes the request object, and calls `BaseHandler.get_response`, which sets the URLconf and calls the chain (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIHandler.__call__`, `django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.get_response`).

The script prefix and the URLconf are both kept for the current thread: the URLconf is `settings.ROOT_URLCONF`, and the prefix is the part of the path the server mounted Django under, with a slash at its end, here `"/"` alone; every URL that `reverse` builds begins with it (`django/urls/base.py:set_script_prefix`, `django/urls/base.py:set_urlconf`).

A signal is a list of receivers, and sending it calls the synchronous receivers in turn and then any asynchronous ones concurrently (`django/dispatch/dispatcher.py:Signal.send`).

The two receivers of `request_started` belong to the database layer: `reset_queries` empties each connection's log of queries, and `close_old_connections` closes any connection that is unusable or past its configured age (`django/db/__init__.py:close_old_connections`).
It wraps the server's input stream in a `LimitedStream` that will not read past the declared content length, and parses nothing else (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIRequest.__init__`).

`WSGIRequest.GET` parses the query string and `WSGIRequest.COOKIES` the `"Cookie"` header, each the first time it is read (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIRequest.GET`, `django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIRequest.COOKIES`).

`WSGIRequest.GET` parses the query string and `WSGIRequest.COOKIES` the `"Cookie"` header, each the first time it is read (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIRequest.GET`, `django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIRequest.COOKIES`).

`WSGIRequest.POST` and `WSGIRequest.FILES` both come from one method, which reads the body only for a `"POST"` of one of the two form types, and otherwise leaves both empty (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest._load_post_and_files`).

Each is built on `MiddlewareMixin`, so each layer's call is `MiddlewareMixin.__call__`: it runs the class's `process_request` if it has one, calls the layer inside unless that returned a response, and runs the class's `process_response` on what comes back (`django/middleware/__init__.py:MiddlewareMixin.__call__`).
Django 1.10 shipped the new style "to solve the lack of strict request/response layering" (`deps:final/0005-improved-middleware.rst`, `docs/releases/1.10.txt`).

**`SecurityMiddleware`** would answer a request that is not secure with a permanent redirect to HTTPS, but only when `settings.SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT` is true, which by default it is not; its work is on the way out (`django/middleware/security.py:SecurityMiddleware.process_request`).
It sets `HttpRequest.session` to a new session store for that key (`django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py:SessionMiddleware.process_request`).

The store does not touch the database: it keeps the key, and the session's data is loaded the first time anything reads it (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.__init__`, `django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase._get_session`).

A host that is not allowed raises `DisallowedHost`, a `SuspiciousOperation`, which the `convert_exception_to_response` wrapper around this layer turns into a 400 response (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`).
When `settings.PREPEND_WWW` is set, it redirects a host without `www.` (`django/middleware/common.py:CommonMiddleware.process_request`, `django/http/request.py:HttpRequest.get_host`).

**`CsrfViewMiddleware`** reads the CSRF cookie, if the request carries one, and puts the secret it holds into `HttpRequest.META` under `"CSRF_COOKIE"` for the rest of the request to use (`django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware.process_request`, `django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware._get_secret`).

It sets `HttpRequest.user` to a `SimpleLazyObject` around a function that will find the user, and `HttpRequest.auser` to its asynchronous twin (`django/contrib/auth/middleware.py:AuthenticationMiddleware.process_request`).

Nothing is looked up until the lazy object is first used: then `get_user` takes the user's id and backend from the session and asks that backend for the user, which is a query (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:get_user`).

The default is `FallbackStorage`, which keeps messages in a cookie and falls back to the session for what does not fit, as [Message storage: `CookieStorage`, `SessionStorage` and `FallbackStorage`](../auth/message-storage.md) tells (`django/contrib/messages/middleware.py:MessageMiddleware.process_request`, `django/contrib/messages/storage/fallback.py:FallbackStorage`).
